TRUTH TO POWER FINAL SCRIPT TX SUNDAY 14th MAY 2023 WITH PROMO’S

Voice over 1
The winter of our discontent has arrived.

The nation is crippled by unprecedented black outs. Livelihoods and food security are under threat

Kusile, our newest power station, was meant to save us. But a fatal design flaw signed off by Eskom in a deal that allegedly benefitted the ruling party, means only one of its boilers is currently working.

Ministers are scrambling, there is no permanent CEO, and its former boss left the country in a hurry, soon after levelling explosive allegations at senior politicians on ENCA.

Bongani
The ANC has not held back in its criticism of you. Do you regret speaking out so forcefully against the party?
ADR
In a certain way, I feel like the little boy in the fairytale who points out that the emperor has no clothes.

Voice over 2
Andre De Ruyter was wary to do this interview. He would not name the politicians he has previously accused, he would speak about the intelligence reports he oversaw, and the book that chronicles his three years at Eskom

Bongani
Where are you?
Andre
I prefer not to disclose my current location.
Bongani
I asked that question because you left this country, ostensibly because you feared for your life. Is that is that correct?
Andre De Ruyter
You know, it's very difficult to separate intelligence from what is true. Uh, but I was made aware that I had reason to be careful, and rather than wait around to see if the intelligence had merit, I decided to be prudent.

Voice over 3
De Ruyter wanted to make a contribution. He calls himself the man in the arena, but like his predecessors he left Eskom before he could succeed.

Andre De Ruyter
Yeah, I think that I obviously would have liked to be seen literally as the knight on the white horse coming in and fixing all the problems. But clearly this is impossible.

Bongani
You're not saying it, but you must be feeling bruised.
Andre De Ruyter
Yes one does start to feel a bit bruised and especially after being accused essentially of treason and being told not to play policeman and suffering an attempted poisoning.

Voice over 4
De Ruyter had hoped to end load shedding in 18 months and get Kusile working.
Energy expert Chris Yelland.

Bongani
Out of ten, where does De Ruyter score?
Chris
Maybe five. I'm not sure that he mobilised that organisation. I'm not sure that he surrounded himself with the right kind of people. He certainly didn't end load shedding. He certainly hadn't yet solved the financial position of Eskom still relying on massive government bailouts- and environmentally Eskom is in deep, deep trouble. Could he have done better? Probably not!

Voice over 5
Busi Mavuso is executive director of Business Leadership SA, and a former Eskom board member

BUSI
I think if the measure is keeping the lights on at all times, then Andre, the board that I served on failed. The current board is failing. Both Minister Pravin Gordhan and Minister Mantashe and President Cyril Ramaphosa failed. So it's not one person's failure.

LINK
Eskom’s headquarters have all the hallmarks of a functioning utility a business park with manicured lawns and tight security, but this calm facade belies the chaos at its power stations

Bongani
When you arrived, your first order of business was to go and see for yourself. What did you find at the power stations?
ADR
I was quite shocked I have to admit. I found power stations that had clearly been neglected. I found processes to manage coal quality, for example, to be either absent or very poorly applied.

Voice over 6
Tutuka- 25 kilometres from Standerton is an important link in the transmission system between Mpumalanga, Western Cape and KZN

ADR
It was clear that Tutuka was a hotbed of corruption. Water tanks were leaking and ash was in abundance everywhere. It was just a really disillusioning experience.

Voice over 7
Hidden by ash at Tutuka, was an entire excavator

Andre
This is one of those surreal moments where you say that this can possibly be true. Who in his right mind would park a large, expensive piece of yellow plant in the middle of an ash dam and then proceed to cover it with ash?

Voice over 8
De Ruyter appointed a new power station manager there, Sello Mametja

ADR
He was viciously threatened. He was maligned, falsely accused, and it was clear that the pushback against any turnaround would be very significant.

Voice over 9
Soon this new manager at Tutuka would uncover a massive fuel oil syndicate

Andre
He followed a truck in the middle of the night. And in so doing, he uncovered a racket, proved to reduce consumption of fuel oil at Tutuka of R100 million rands a month.

Voice over 10
De Ruyter estimates Eskom loses about a billion rand a month through corruption and theft

Andre De Ruyter
It was one commodity, one power station and it was R100 million rand per month. So you can imagine if you start multiplying that across 15 Power stations and you look at thousands of commodities that Eskom buys– you can imagine the size of the looting that goes on.

LINK
Corruption, sabotage, state capture, every South African sitting in the dark knows there is a lot wrong with Eskom. But few of us realise how basic some of the problems are

Voice over 11
Without consistent and correct coal specifications - power stations fail and we end up in the dark.

Bongani
Burning rocks instead of coal?
Andre De Ruyter
Ya that is fairly difficult to do. -boulders the size of your head, that would go into mills literally causing the mills to explode. And this is corruption.

Voice over 12
At Kusile, he says it was a constant problem

Andre De Ruyter
And it took an extraordinary amount of time and effort first of all to persuade people that coal quality is important which says something about the focus of the organisation.
Bongani
Hold on! They did not know?!
Andre De Ruyter
They thought that it was somebody else's problem. That it was the power station general managers problem. And the power station general Manager said, oh well, you know, I have no control over coal quality, that's the job of the primary energy division. And I kept walking around saying chaps- coal is your single most important process variable in running a power station. And we are not controlling it!

LINK
Being at the helm of Eskom is not just ensuring there is coal at the power stations, or keeping the lights on, but you have to walk a delicate tightrope, managing different stakeholders, pulling in all sorts of directions.

Chris Yelland
I mean, you've got the Minister of Public Enterprises, you have the Minister of Mineral Resources and Energy, you have the Minister of Finance, you have the Minister of Forestry, Fisheries and the Environment, you have the Cogta Minister.

Voice over 13
Add to that a new minister of electricity! And somewhere governance gets lost.
Political analyst Tessa Dooms

Tessa
if you focus on the governance side rather than the smokes and the mirrors, we would have a lot more inside information and accountability

Voice over 14
Dooms says De Ruyter should have challenged the politicians earlier

Tessa
His job was to go to parliament, the place where he is accountable, and the place where those very politicians are accountable and give the public the information that we need in order to solve this crisis. Because the one thing that I will say over and over is that no one can solve the crisis until we lift the hood of what's happening at Eskom and we actually see what's under the hood

Voice over 15
In the beginning, De Ruyter had the support of public enterprises Minister Pravin Gordhan and President Ramaphosa.
Ramaphosa encouraged De Ruyter to pursue renewable energy, but that put him on a collision course with energy Minister Gwede Mantashe who is a coal man through and through

Bongani
I quote: “For the Minister of Energy to be the cause of an energy crisis that has been going on for 15 years is beyond words.”
ADR
I agree it is beyond words.

Voice over 16
De Ruyter was pursuing renewables and 8.5 billion dollars for South Africa’s just transition Mantashe wanted to build more coal fired power stations. He has said that renewable energy costs Eskom more money than the government lets on, which is why he doesn’t think it’s the best solution for Eskom

In a high level meeting De Ruyter wrote a note to self

Bongani : What did you write in your note?
Andre De Ruyter
I said Gwede is completely terrifying. And I said it / because listening to what Mantashe says it was completely at odds with the trajectory of where the Global energy environment is going.

Voice over 17
Minister Mantashe blamed Eskom for withholding power, but as Yelland points out - its Mantashe’s job to ensure South Africa has enough power. It's in his performance agreement

Chris
Minister Mantashe is responsible for Eskom's energy availability factor. The target set is written out in black and white, and the same applies to new generation capacity. It's clearly minister Mantashe’s responsibility.

Voice over 18 defer to Chris
A high energy availability factor- the percentage of the Eskom fleet there is in the system, is crucial to end loadshedding. Right now it’s not even at 60%

Chris
The Eskom EAF is a measure over a period of time of the percentage of the Eskom fleet of generators that was available for duty

Bongani
Andre De Ruyter says one of the pressures he faced was getting the energy availability factor up to 70%. And he couldn't look the president in the eye and tell him it was possible.
Chris
It's not possible! He's right. The chairman of Eskom announced targets. The first target has already not been met. At the end of March 2023, the energy availability factor was 56% and not 60%. There is no way that it's going to be 65% by the end of the financial year, ending to 31st of March 2024. And there's no way that 70% is going to be achieved.


Voice over 19
De Ruyter writes that the cost to the country of embedded criminality at Eskom is incalculable.

Andre De Ruyter
If a power station manager's children have to be delivered to school by armed guards. This is extraordinary.

Voice over 20
The fight against the crooks he says, was like holding back a Tsunami with his bare hands

Andre
I was really in fairly desperate straits at that time in terms of getting very little support from the South African police services, from intelligence services. It was quite clear that the SSA had some knowledge of a campaign of sabotage, but they chose not to pursue it extensively because of COVID, and SAPS were in their own words unaware of any of these activities taking place, or at least the National Police Commissioner was unaware.

LINK
With his back against the wall, Andre had to demonstrate what he believed was going on at Eskom and he needed evidence.

Andre:
What was I supposed to do? Was I supposed to again go to the same entities that had repeatedly failed to support? Or was I put in a position where in order to do my job, which was to protect the assets of Eskom, where I needed to gather intelligence that I could submit for the police and others to investigate properly, as is their lawful duty. And in fact Minister Gordhan said , you know, you need to have some intelligence gathering capability.

LINK
But he turned to the worst possible source - a private investigation firm using former apartheid era operatives

Voice over 21
George Fivas Forensic and risk was founded by this former national police commissioner. Forensic investigation is one of its services

Bongani
This outfit. George Fivas?!
Andre
He uses former national intelligence operatives. I did not do a due diligence on all of them, nor did I think it was necessary for me to do so, based on the reputation of the proprietor of the business, the person in charge, George FIVAS.


Voice over 22
But if he had, he would discovered that Fivas appointed an apartheid era assassin to manage the private investigation; a revelation published by News 24 on the morning of De Ruyter’s much anticipated appearance in Parliament last month

Bongani
When you've got former apartheid intelligence operatives pointing fingers at the current political establishment. Surely you could have anticipated that would be problematic?
Andre
Yes, people have significant skeletons in their cupboards and I don’t profess to be an apologist for that at all. But to disregard the findings because of the history I think is also not appropriate and is not a smart move to do.

Voice over 23
Members of Business Leadership paid R50 million for the investigation.
Busi
And I certainly don't think that they made an error of judgement actually if we had to do this all over again as BLSA we would

Voice over 24
But Mavuso acknowledges in this case, things could have been more thorough

Busi
You know, when I bring a service provider on board and this is true for all companies, I don't normally say to them, give me a list of all your employees in your organisation so I can see if any of them are apartheid spies. That is not done in the ordinary course of business, but for an operation like this -I absolutely agree. We could have done a better job in checking and vetting who is actually behind George Fivas forensic and risk

Voice over 25
Carte Blanche has seen the intelligence files, and was underwhelmed by the evidence presented.

Bongani
Andre, it's fair to ask you, what did you do? We have, as Carte Blanche, spoken to some of the operatives you were working with. We have looked at their files and their documents. Some of the information contained there is outlandish. This is not stuff you could put in a docket and hope to prosecute a case?

Andre De Ruyter
Yeah, if you look at the difference between intelligence and evidence, When I read through some of the intelligence reports clearly there is an amount of exaggeration there.






Voice over 26
Fivas told Carte Blanche that after the News 24 articles, they are considering their available options to protect the reputational damage to their company, and would therefore not be granting media interviews at this stage

Bongani
So here we are. We still don't know the names. You wouldn't say that to Scopa. Do you see the difficulty that South Africans must contend with? We're sitting in the dark, corruption and criminality is being blamed, but it's nameless, faceless, shadowy figures and there's no case to prove.
Andre
I don't think there is no case to prove. I think what is important is that the cases be investigated properly.

Bongani
Will this investigation be the ultimate black mark on his legacy?
Chris Yelland
It has seriously impacted his reputation and his credibility. No question about it, in my mind

Voice over 27
By September last year, De Ruyter writes, that he could feel the political support eroding beneath his feet. Soon after he threw in the towel

Bongani
If you were to rate yourself out of ten. What score would you give yourself?
Andre
I think between a six and a seven probably. I did not solve load shedding. I think solving load shedding is going to be a long term exercise. I did not address all of the corruption, An unqualified success? Absolutely not. Miserable failure. I think that's being too harsh.

Voice over 28
And as the grid teeters close to collapse De Ruyter’s allegations are still reverberating through parliament ( B to advise)

Andre
My question would be, if I had done nothing would the criminal justice system have been galvanised into action. I am sceptical.

THE END






PROMO ONE 11 seconds
blackouts are crippling the country. Ministers are scrambling and the former Eskom CEO says corruption and theft is costing Eskom a billion rand a month

PROMO TWO
Former Eskom CEO Andre De Ruyter wanted to leave a legacy that ended corruption at Eskom
Bongani
So here we are. We still don't know the names. You wouldn't say that to Scopa. Do you see the difficulty that South Africans must contend with? We're sitting in the dark, corruption and criminality is being blamed, but it's nameless, faceless, shadowy figures and there's no case to prove.
Andre
I don't think there is no case to prove. I think what is important is that the cases be investigated properly.

PROMO THREE
Former Eskom CEO blew the whistle on the rot at the power utility, leaving parliament and law enforcement to sift fact from fiction. Now De Ruyter’s book tells his story of three years at Megawatt Park.
ADR
In a certain way, I feel like the little boy In the fairy-tale who points out that the emperor has no clothes.
